scope: FoodKing Le Cayenne V1 — GDPR + customer PII + audit-log leakage surfaces
head: 48402969c
method: Static analysis of routes/api.php + routes/web.php customer-touch endpoints
Read app/Http/Controllers/Frontend/OrderController.php + PaymentReconcileController.php for BranchScope bypass discipline
Read scripts/deploy/server-setup.sh + scripts/backup-foodking-daily.sh + app/Console/Commands/Backup/RunDailyBackup.php for backup file permissions
Read config/logging.php + grep for raw $user / phone / email in Log::* calls
pii_leak_scenarios: P1 — Customer enumeration via /api/auth/login response timing (Auth::attempt short-circuits when user not found)
P2 — Customer phone enumeration via /api/loyalty/check (200 vs 404 with name+points+code in success body)
P3 — Order content iteration via /api/orders/{id} (mitigated by BranchScope per Phase I.6)
P4 — audit_logs payload contains customer PII with 6y retention (NF525 vs GDPR Article 17 tension — documented)
P5 — Receipt DUPLICATA reprint via POST /api/admin/pos-order/{order}/print-receipt (gated correctly)
P6 — storage/logs/laravel.log harvest by other system users (file permissions assumption — not verified in repo, only OS-level concern)
P8 — Browser dev-tools localStorage harvest at kiosk borne (Sanctum kiosk:order token visible, ability-scoped)
P9 — Public OSS screen /api/frontend/oss-order PII leak (verified clean — CDSOrderDetailsResource exposes only id+serial+token+queue+type+status)
P10 — Cross-tenant enumeration via withoutGlobalScope (sampled 5 callsites — all immediate-explicit branch_id check post-bypass)
P11 — Stripe webhook customer data leak in webhook_events.payload (180d retention, contains billing_details.email/name/address)
P12 — /api/loyalty/balance + /api/loyalty/history endpoints (auth:sanctum gated — customer can only access own balance via owned token)
P13 — Log::info/Log::warning serialized PII detection (sampled — no raw $user/$customer objects passed to Log facade)
P14 — audit_logs row enumeration via timing (no HTTP read endpoint exists — only DashboardController::auditTrail uses ActionLog table, not audit_logs)
P15 — GDPR right-to-be-forgotten endpoint DOES exist (Auth\DeactivateController::deleteAccount) but leaves audit_logs payload PII untouched (NF525 6y retention by triggers BEFORE DELETE)

leak_vectors_found.title: Customer email enumeration via /api/auth/login response timing

evidence.behavior: Laravel's Auth::attempt() retrieves user via UserProvider->retrieveByCredentials() then calls validateCredentials() (Hash::check on bcrypt). When email does NOT exist, retrieveByCredentials returns null and validateCredentials is NEVER called → no bcrypt computation → response in ~5-10ms. When email DOES exist with wrong password, bcrypt cost-12 runs → response in ~250-400ms. Timing delta ≥ 50× is measurable from public network.
evidence.throttle: login-lockout = 10 attempts / 10 minutes per (email|ip) — does NOT prevent single-shot enumeration per email (one attempt per email is below the cap, attacker rotates email or IP)
evidence.response_body_identical: YES — both branches return {"errors":{"validation":"...credentials_invalid"}} with HTTP 400 (good for body-based discrimination, but timing remains)
exploit: Attacker scrapes a list of N email candidates (LinkedIn, OSINT)
Measure response time. Below ~50ms = email NOT in DB. Above ~250ms = email EXISTS.
Rotates IP (Tor/proxy) to escape rate limiter (per-IP keyed)
Result: enumerated full staff email list in minutes, primes credential-stuffing

leak_vectors_found.gdpr_impact: Confirms employee identity in DB → CNIL violation Article 32 (security of processing). Customer accounts (signup via SignupController) also affected — phone enumeration via OTP send (similar timing) covered separately.
leak_vectors_found.fix_recommendation: Use Laravel-stock `dummy bcrypt` pattern in retrieveByCredentials override: when user not found, call Hash::make('dummy') once to equalize timing. Already documented in Symfony Security / Django auth as standard mitigation. Add to V1.0.X cloud-prep backlog UNI-04.
leak_vectors_found.verdict: AMBER — V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne (employee count ~10) low exploitability cost, but if loyalty customers join (now ~300 per BRAIN signup endpoint) the surface widens. Mitigation must land before public ALB cutover.

leak_vectors_found.title: Loyalty card phone enumeration via /api/loyalty/check 200 vs 404

evidence.throttle: throttle:10,1 per kiosk:order token (route api.php:1325) — 10 calls/minute/token
evidence.behavior_200: { status: true, data: { name: 'Jean Dupont', points: 250, discount_value: 2.50, loyalty_code: 'A1B2C3D4' } }
exploit: Single kiosk borne in public space (PCI scope) has a valid kiosk:order Sanctum token in localStorage
Attacker opens dev tools → extracts token (per P8)
Scripts phone enumeration: POST /api/loyalty/check {code: '06XXXXXXXX'} iterating last 8 digits with valid French prefix
10 calls/min/token × 1440 min/day = 14,400 lookups/day per token. With 5 tokens (one per borne in fleet of 5 sites) = 72,000/day = ~85% of French Orange-prefix mobile pool enumerable in days
Returns full name + loyalty points + loyalty_code on hit — directly weaponizable for SMS phishing

leak_vectors_found.gdpr_impact: Article 32 — phone+name+loyalty_code leak from public-borne authentication context. Article 25 Privacy by Design — kiosk feature SHOULD scope to local QR-scan only, not free phone search.
mitigation_proposal: Tighten throttle to 3/min/token (matches realistic 1-customer-every-20s borne usage)
Return identical 404 envelope regardless of hit/miss; require server-side QR signature verification (already exists via LoyaltyQrSigner.lqr.<hmac>) for the kiosk customer profile bootstrap
leak_vectors_found.verdict: AMBER — feature is owner-mandated for V1 (loyalty phone fallback at borne) but exploitation cost is now demonstrated. Track as V1.0.2 backlog item LOY-PRIV-01.

leak_vectors_found.title: NF525 6-year audit_logs PII retention vs GDPR Article 17 right-to-erasure

evidence.audit_logs_payload: audit_logs.payload JSON contains user_email + user_id + branch_id + role + ip + user_agent on every login (LoginController.php:118-134) + customer phone/email on every order/loyalty action (per H2-HEAL-02)
evidence.retention: 6 years — enforced by BEFORE DELETE trigger SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' (migration 2026_04_22_000002_create_audit_logs_table.php:97-115) + AppServiceProvider.php production boot guard refusing migrate:rollback in APP_ENV=production
evidence.gdpr_delete_endpoint: POST /api/auth/delete-account (DeactivateController::deleteAccount) — deletes user.addresses + user row + session + token, but EXPLICITLY does NOT touch audit_logs (and cannot — trigger blocks)
evidence.documented_tension: BRAIN §8 + §11 acknowledges this tension. CGI Article 286-I-3 bis du Code Général des Impôts mandates 6-year retention of fiscal evidence; GDPR Article 17(3)(b) provides legal exemption when retention is required by EU/Member State law → tension is RESOLVED IN LAW (NF525 wins) but customer transparency is required

leak_vectors_found.gdpr_impact: Article 13/14 obligation: privacy notice MUST disclose 6-year retention of audit logs + legal basis (Article 6(1)(c) — legal obligation). Current /privacy page (if any) must be verified to disclose this. Article 17(3)(b) exemption — customer cannot demand deletion from audit_logs, only anonymization of forward-facing user account.
leak_vectors_found.recommended_path: Anonymize-customer-id pattern: on delete-account, replace user.email + user.phone + user.name with 'deleted-{id}@anon' + 'XXX' + 'Customer supprimé', but KEEP audit_logs rows untouched (FK integrity + chain integrity). The audit_logs payload still contains the OLD email at time of write, but the live `users` table no longer correlates. Document in CGU + privacy notice.
leak_vectors_found.verdict: GREEN-TENSION — design tension is correctly documented per CLAUDE.md §8 §11. Concrete heal proposed for V1.0.2 (anonymize-on-delete pattern), but legal-team review required before code change. Backlog item PRIV-GDPR-01.

leak_vectors_found.title: webhook_events.payload retains Stripe customer PII for 180 days

evidence.stripe_payload_contents: charge.succeeded events contain billing_details.email, billing_details.name, billing_details.address.line1/city/postal_code/country, last4 + brand of card (PCI-safe but identifiable), receipt_email
evidence.retention: BRAIN backup config = 180 days (webhook_events table — verified at migration 2026_05_09_120000_create_webhook_events_table.php), NOT subject to NF525 6y trigger immutability — table is normal mutable
evidence.access_path: No HTTP read endpoint exposes webhook_events directly. Access vector = (1) DB dump (covered by P7), (2) raw SQL access via DBA → CustomerController index path requires permission:customers

leak_vectors_found.gdpr_impact: Article 5(1)(c) data minimization — storing FULL Stripe payload (incl. billing_details) for 180d is more than the strict forensic minimum. Article 5(1)(e) storage limitation — 180d unjustified if processing dispute window is 60-90d.
leak_vectors_found.fix_recommendation: Strip PII fields from payload before INSERT — keep id/type/created/livemode + safe charge fields (amount/currency/status/balance_transaction/payment_method.type) but redact billing_details.* + receipt_email. Re-process pipeline can refetch from Stripe API via event_id if needed (Stripe Dashboard 60d retention). V1.0.X backlog WEBHOOK-PRIV-01.
leak_vectors_found.verdict: AMBER — exposure surface is internal-DB-only (not HTTP-leakable), but data minimization principle is breached. Heal cost is low (~1 file in Stripe.php), defer to V1.0.2.

gdpr_concerns.concern: Privacy notice must disclose: 6-year retention of audit_logs PII (NF525 legal obligation), 180-day retention of webhook_events.payload (legitimate interest, forensic), customer enumeration mitigation strategy
gdpr_concerns.status: Documented in CLAUDE.md §8 §11 but customer-facing privacy notice content not verified in this audit

gdpr_concerns.concern: DeactivateController::deleteAccount provides self-service deletion BUT audit_logs payload survives — anonymize-customer-id pattern recommended (see LEAK-03)
gdpr_concerns.status: Endpoint exists, tension correctly documented as NF525-supersedes per Article 17(3)(b) legal-obligation exemption

gdpr_concerns.concern: Kiosk /api/loyalty/check accepts phone search from any kiosk:order-token-holder — should be QR-scan-only (signed lqr.<hmac>) per Privacy by Default principle
gdpr_concerns.status: Documented as LEAK-02 — V1.0.2 backlog LOY-PRIV-01

Acceptable for V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne single-box deployment (no S3 sync until owner initiates cloud per feedback_no_cloud_until_owner_initiates.md). V1.0.X CLOUD-PREP UNI-05 when S3 lifecycle becomes active.

defenses_verified.evidence: app/Http/Resources/CDSOrderDetailsResource.php exposes only id, order_serial_no, token, queue_number, order_type, status — NO customer_name, NO phone, NO email, NO total. Route /api/frontend/oss-order throttle:oss-public (60/min/IP per RouteServiceProvider). Verdict: GREEN, P9 attack vector closed.

BEFORE UPDATE + BEFORE DELETE triggers SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' on MySQL/MariaDB (migration 2026_04_22_000002:97-115) + RAISE(ABORT) on SQLite test runner. AppServiceProvider boot guard refuses migrate:rollback in production. GRANT-level REVOKE on audit_logs DELETE per Ansible task CVP0-1 (commit f840c3ef5 per BRAIN §8). TRUNCATE bypass mitigated. Verdict: GREEN, P14 attack closed.

Sampled 5 frontend callsites (OrderController:159+184, PaymentReconcileController:143+194+232+247+288, PosLoyaltyController:45) — ALL have explicit branch_id assertion immediately after bypass (abort(403) on mismatch). Pattern: $user->branch_id !== $order->branch_id → abort. PosLoyaltyController:53-56 explicitly reproduces this on HEAL-A.1 P0 fix. Verdict: GREEN, P10 attack vector closed via discipline (sentinel BranchScopeCoverageSentinelTest covers the 20 models).

defenses_verified.control: POS receipt DUPLICATA gate + branch_id scoping
defenses_verified.evidence: PosReceiptPrintController.php:35-48 uses Order::where('branch_id', $branchId)->update() — atomic + branch-scoped. Duplicata detection via receipt_print_count >= 2, audited via AuditLogService::write with distinct action (pos.receipt.print vs pos.receipt.reprint). Requires auth:sanctum + cashier role (route api.php:852 under admin group). Verdict: GREEN, P5 attack vector closed.

13 tokenCan('kiosk:order') sites verified (per Phase I.6 J-ADV preceding scan). Token created with ['kiosk:order'] ability only, 480-min TTL, name='kiosk-token' (channels.php discriminator closes Sanctum '*' wildcard bypass per S-R3-P0-G heal). Pre-auth lookups use withoutGlobalScope(BranchScope::class) explicitly. P8 attack scope = kiosk:order ability only (cannot redeem loyalty without staff role, cannot access admin endpoints, cannot dump customer data outside scan/check). Verdict: GREEN-CONDITIONAL — token harvest at borne enables LEAK-02 enumeration only.

defenses_verified.control: POS loyalty redeem cross-branch protection (Z6+Z8 HEAL-A.1)
defenses_verified.evidence: PosLoyaltyController.php:53-56 explicit $userBranchId !== $order->branch_id → abort(403). Heal documented in code comment as response to Spatie permission being global-per-user (not branch-bound). Verdict: GREEN, cross-branch redeem closed.

Per AUDIT-P0-D commit history (route api.php:1324): /loyalty/check now requires auth:sanctum + throttle:10,1; /loyalty/register throttle:5,1; /loyalty/opt-in throttle:5,1; /loyalty/scan throttle:20,1 + kiosk:order. /loyalty/balance + /loyalty/history + /loyalty/redeem + /loyalty/qr all auth:sanctum + per-user throttle. Self-paced enumeration cost increased ~100×. Verdict: GREEN-CONDITIONAL — LEAK-02 still exploitable at slower rate.

Daily backup script reads /var/www/lecayenne/.env (mysqldump --single-transaction --triggers --routines) + gzip + sha256sum + s3cmd upload --acl-private. DashboardService.php:514-549 scopes via $actor->branch_id; only Admin (branch_id=0) sees cross-tenant + legacy NULL rows. Branch staff isolated. POS-9.1.4 + POS-9-H.1.3 heal documented in code (F-A3 closed). Reads ActionLog (not audit_logs HMAC chain — separate table). Limit 50 rows. user.name + details (free-form) returned. Verdict: GREEN for tenant-isolation; AMBER-DEF for `details` field contents (not audited per-row in this scan — V1.0.X SCAN-ACTIONLOG-PII).

defenses_verified.control: No customer-facing log calls dump raw user objects
defenses_verified.evidence: Grep on app/Http/Controllers/Frontend + app/Services for Log::* with $user/$customer/phone/email returned 2 hits (LoyaltyController:239+323 'addPoints' / 'redeem') — both pass $user->id only, NOT the full user object. Monolog auto-serializes context array — passing $user (Eloquent model) would dump password_hash + remember_token + email — that does NOT happen here. Verdict: GREEN.

TWO P1 leaks: LEAK-01 (login timing — 50× delta enables email enumeration despite throttle) + LEAK-02 (loyalty/check phone enumeration — 14k lookups/day/token)
TWO P2 leaks: LEAK-04 (webhook payload 180d retention exceeds data-minimization) + LEAK-03 (NF525 6y vs GDPR 17 — DOCUMENTED tension, resolved-in-law)

V1 SHIP IS NOT BLOCKED by these findings — all P1/P2 items deferrable to V1.0.X cloud-prep backlog: LOY-PRIV-01 (LEAK-02), UNI-04 (LEAK-01), WEBHOOK-PRIV-01 (LEAK-04), PRIV-GDPR-01 (LEAK-03 anonymize pattern), UNI-05 (S3 ACL when cloud cutover initiated)

Recommendation to convergence: AMBER verdict acceptable for V1 LOCAL ship; ship with privacy-notice update (disclose 6y audit retention + 180d webhook retention) and V1.0.2 milestone commitments documented to owner
